title: Explaining how
job: Steps and instructions in order, and what they are for
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

allowedTenses: imperativo, familiar and polite — the module's new mood
infinitive, after non in a familiar order and after per
present indicative, L1-M6's, where the familiar order borrows its shape (vai)

rules.text: THE IMPERATIVE'S ENDINGS ARE CROSSED, AND THE CROSSING IS THE WHOLE DIFFICULTY. Speaking to a friend, an -are verb ends in -a (gira, aspetta, guarda) and an -ere or -ire verb ends in -i (prendi, apri, senti). Speaking politely the two swap over: -are takes -i (giri, firmi, scusi) and -ere and -ire take -a (prenda, senta, apra). One and the same ending is therefore familiar on one class of verb and polite on the other. Learn it as the swap; two separate lists are exactly what a learner merges.

ENGLISH GIVES YOU THE SHAPE FOR FREE. Gira a destra is Turn right word for word and in the same order: the verb comes first, no pronoun is written, and nothing about the SHAPE has to be unlearned. What English does not have is the second imperative — it has one, Italian has two. A learner who has only ever met the polite forms (L2-M1's scusi and senta, L2-M4's vada, prenda and giri) will say Giri to a friend and sound like a ticket office.

A NEGATIVE ORDER TO A FRIEND IS non PLUS THE INFINITIVE. Non toccare, non aprire, non dimenticare — not the positive form with non stuck in front of it. It looks nothing like the tocca or the apri beside it, and that is the point at which English gives no help: do not touch is one construction for everybody. The polite imperative keeps its own shape under negation (non tocchi, non apra), so the two registers part company here.

PURPOSE IS per PLUS THE INFINITIVE, NEVER a. English to — meaning in order to — comes out as per: Premi il tasto per uscire, Questo tasto serve per uscire. L3-M2 taught per as for in Lavoro per una ditta italiana; this is the same word doing a second job, which is why it earns no new row. A learner who has met vado a mangiare will reach for a here: a plus an infinitive follows a verb of motion and never states a purpose.

THE POLITE IMPERATIVE IS BORROWED, AND THE OBJECT STAYS A SEPARATE WORD. metta, apra, aspetti and dica are not a form of their own: they are a slice of the congiuntivo, a mood this course opens at L4-M5. Take them here as fixed shapes to be said. And keep every object beside the verb — dica il numero, metta il documento — because the joined-on pronoun forms (dimmi, prendilo) belong to L5 with the rest of clitic attachment.

sentences.display: Prima apri la finestra, poi chiudi la porta
sentences.cue: First open the window, then close the door
sentences.literal: First open the window, then close the door

words.note: The familiar imperative of aprire. An -ire verb takes -i here, which is the very ending the polite form uses on -are verbs.
The familiar imperative of chiudere. -ere takes -i too, so apri and chiudi rhyme; the polite pair would be apra and chiuda.
Feminine. aprire la finestra is the ordinary way to say air the room, and una finestra sulla strada is a window onto the street.

sentences.trap: English can front the pronoun in an order — you open the window — and Italian cannot. The verb stands alone and its ending alone says who is being told.
sentences.sound: PREE-ma AH-pree la fee-NES-tra, poy KYOO-dee la POR-ta. chiudi begins KYOO: chi is k plus i, never the ch of church.

variations.display: Prima chiudi la porta, poi apri la finestra
variations.cue: First close the door, then open the window
variations.changed: the two steps swapped round

variations.cue: Open the window, please
variations.changed: one step, softened with L1-M8's per favore

variations.cue: Do not open the window
variations.changed: negative, so the verb drops back to the infinitive

mistake.display: Prima apra la finestra, poi chiudi la porta
mistake.why: apra is the polite form and chiudi the familiar one; a single order cannot use both. To a friend it is apri ... chiudi.

sentences.usage: Handing a friend or a flatmate two steps in the order they happen.
sentences.mnemonic: -are ends in -a for a friend; everything else ends in -i.

sentences.display: Per prima cosa metti la pentola sul fuoco
sentences.cue: First of all put the pot on the heat
sentences.literal: For first thing put the pot on-the fire

words.note: Three words, one fixed phrase: the first thing to do. It never changes shape, and it opens a list of steps where prima on its own would also do.
The familiar imperative of mettere. -ere takes -i, so it is metti; the polite form metta is S09's, with the endings crossed over.
Feminine. The deep cooking pot that sits on the stove; the flat frying pan is a padella.

words.cue: fire; the heat of a stove
words.note: Masculine. On a stove it is the burner and the heat on it: sul fuoco is on the heat, a fuoco basso on a low flame.

sentences.trap: per prima cosa is frozen: never per la prima cosa, never per prime cose. Nothing inside it agrees with anything.
sentences.sound: per PREE-ma KO-za MET-tee la PEN-to-la sul FWO-ko. The double t of metti is held: MET-tee, not ME-tee.

variations.display: Prima metti la pentola sul fuoco
variations.cue: First put the pot on the heat
variations.changed: prima on its own, shorter and just as ordinary

variations.display: Per prima cosa guarda la ricetta
variations.cue: First of all look at the recipe
variations.changed: a different opening step

variations.cue: Put the pot on the heat — politely
variations.changed: polite, so mettere's -ere swings to -a

mistake.display: Per prima cosa metta la pentola sul fuoco, poi aggiungi il sale
mistake.why: metta is polite and aggiungi is familiar, so the two halves address two different people. Pick one register and keep it to the end.

sentences.usage: Reading a recipe out to somebody who is doing the cooking.
sentences.mnemonic: mettere is -ere, so a friend gets metti.

sentences.display: Aggiungi il sale, poi aspetta dieci minuti
sentences.cue: Add the salt, then wait ten minutes
sentences.literal: Add the salt, then wait ten minutes

words.note: The familiar imperative of aggiungere, an -ere verb, so -i. The gg is soft before i: ad-JOON-jee.
Masculine, and with no plural in this sense. The same four letters are also he or she goes up, from salire; the article tells them apart.
The familiar imperative of aspettare, an -are verb, so -a. The polite form is aspetti, which is the ending a learner expects for a friend.
Masculine. dieci minuti is ten minutes and un minuto is one; un momento does the same job when the length does not matter.

sentences.trap: aspettare takes its object directly: aspetta dieci minuti, never aspetta per dieci minuti. The for of English wait for does not cross over.
sentences.sound: ad-JOON-jee il SA-le, poy as-PET-ta DYE-chee mee-NOO-tee. gg before i is the j of jam.

variations.cue: Add the salt and wait
variations.changed: e in place of poi, and no length of time

variations.display: Aspetta dieci minuti, poi aggiungi il sale
variations.cue: Wait ten minutes, then add the salt
variations.changed: the two steps in the other order

variations.cue: Wait ten minutes, please — politely
variations.changed: polite, so aspettare's -are swings to -i

mistake.display: Aggiunga il sale, poi aspetta dieci minuti
mistake.why: aggiunga is the polite form standing beside the familiar aspetta. To a friend the pair is aggiungi ... aspetta.

sentences.usage: Talking a friend through a recipe step by step.
sentences.mnemonic: One -ere verb in -i, one -are verb in -a: that is the familiar side.

sentences.display: Non toccare la pentola, è molto calda
sentences.cue: Do not touch the pot, it is very hot
sentences.literal: Not to-touch the pot, it-is very hot

words.cue: do not touch — to a friend
words.note: One shape for every negative order to a friend: non plus the plain infinitive. It looks nothing like the positive tocca standing beside it.

sentences.trap: The positive is tocca and the negative is non toccare — the verb changes shape completely. English keeps one form for both: touch it, do not touch it.
sentences.sound: non tok-KA-re la PEN-to-la, e MOL-to KAL-da. The cc of toccare is held: tok-KA-re.

variations.cue: Do not open the window
variations.changed: a different verb in the same non plus infinitive frame

variations.cue: Do not forget the salt
variations.changed: L2-M8's dimenticare, negated the same way

variations.cue: Do not touch the heat
variations.changed: a different thing not to touch

mistake.why: non tocca is he does not touch. A negative order to a friend is non plus the infinitive: non toccare.

sentences.usage: Warning somebody off something hot, sharp or fragile.
sentences.mnemonic: Say no to a friend and the verb goes back to the dictionary.

sentences.display: Guarda le istruzioni della ricetta e non dimenticare il sale
sentences.cue: Look at the recipe's instructions and do not forget the salt
sentences.literal: Look the instructions of-the recipe and not to-forget the salt

words.note: The familiar imperative of guardare, an -are verb, so -a. guardare takes its object with no preposition: guarda le istruzioni.
Feminine, and normally plural like the English. It covers the leaflet in the box as well as the steps themselves.
Feminine, and it does both jobs: the recipe you cook from and the prescription the doctor writes.

sentences.trap: English looks AT something and Italian does not: guarda le istruzioni, never guarda a le istruzioni. The preposition simply is not there.
sentences.sound: GWAR-da le ee-stroo-TSYO-nee del-la ree-CHET-ta e non dee-men-tee-KA-re il SA-le. The zi of istruzioni is ts.

variations.cue: Look at the recipe
variations.changed: the first half on its own

variations.cue: Do not look at the instructions
variations.changed: negative, so guardare drops back to the infinitive

variations.display: Guarda le istruzioni e aggiungi il sale
variations.cue: Look at the instructions and add the salt
variations.changed: a positive second step in place of the warning

mistake.why: guardare needs no preposition, and a le would not be written that way in any case. It is guarda le istruzioni.

sentences.usage: Pointing a friend at the written steps rather than explaining them.
sentences.mnemonic: guarda looks straight at it, with no a in between.

sentences.display: Prima gira a destra, poi vai dritto
sentences.cue: First turn right, then go straight on
sentences.literal: First turn to right, then go straight

words.note: The familiar imperative of girare, an -are verb, so -a. The polite giri is L2-M4's, in Giri a destra, and it is the -i a learner expects for a friend.

sentences.trap: vai is L1-M6's present tense doing double duty: the familiar order of andare is the form you already know, with nothing new to learn. The polite one is vada, taught at L2-M4.
sentences.sound: PREE-ma JEE-ra a DES-tra, poy vai DREET-to. gira is JEE-ra: g before i is soft.

variations.display: Gira a destra e poi vai dritto
variations.cue: Turn right and then go straight on
variations.changed: e in place of the prima and poi frame

variations.display: Prima vai dritto, poi gira a destra
variations.cue: First go straight on, then turn right
variations.changed: the two steps swapped round

variations.cue: Turn right, then wait
variations.changed: a different second step

mistake.display: Prima giri a destra, poi vai dritto
mistake.why: giri is the polite form — L2-M4's Giri a destra. To a friend girare's -are takes -a: gira.

sentences.usage: Giving a friend directions on foot or from the passenger seat.
sentences.mnemonic: girare is -are, so a friend hears gira.

sentences.display: Premi il tasto verde per uscire
sentences.cue: Press the green button to get out
sentences.literal: Press the button green for to-go-out

words.note: The familiar imperative of premere, an -ere verb, so -i; the polite form is prema. premere is the verb a machine's instructions use for a button.
Masculine. A key on a keyboard or a button you press on a panel; the round button on a coat is a bottone.

sentences.trap: Purpose is per plus the infinitive and never a. vado a mangiare is a verb of motion; per uscire is a reason, and a would be wrong here.
sentences.sound: PRE-mee il TAS-to VER-de per oo-SHEE-re. uscire is oo-SHEE-re: sci is sh.

variations.cue: Press the green button
variations.changed: the order alone, with no purpose attached

variations.display: Premi il tasto rosso per uscire
variations.cue: Press the red button to get out
variations.changed: a different button, using L2-M3's rosso

variations.cue: Do not press the green button
variations.changed: negative, so premere drops back to the infinitive

mistake.display: Premi il tasto verde a uscire
mistake.why: purpose never takes a. It is premi il tasto verde per uscire.

sentences.usage: At a door, a lift or a ticket machine, telling somebody which control to use.
sentences.mnemonic: per plus the infinitive is English's in order to.

sentences.cue: This button is for getting out

words.note: servire plus per plus an infinitive: what a thing is FOR. Plural things take servono per. It answers the question a che serve?

sentences.trap: English turns the purpose into an -ing form — for getting out — and Italian keeps the infinitive: per uscire.
sentences.sound: KWES-to TAS-to SER-ve per oo-SHEE-re. serve is two syllables, SER-ve.

variations.display: Il tasto verde serve per uscire
variations.cue: The green button is for getting out
variations.changed: the button named by its colour instead of pointed at

variations.display: Questo tasto non serve per uscire
variations.cue: This button is not for getting out
variations.changed: negative, and non goes in front of serve, not in front of per

variations.cue: It is for getting out
variations.changed: the subject dropped, as Italian freely does

mistake.why: in this sense servire takes per: serve per uscire. servire a exists, but it means to be of use to somebody.

sentences.usage: Explaining what a control on a machine actually does.
sentences.mnemonic: serve per — what a thing serves FOR.

sentences.display: Scusi, metta il documento sul tavolo e dica il numero
sentences.cue: Excuse me, put the document on the table and say the number
sentences.literal: Excuse-me, put the document on-the table and say the number

words.note: The polite imperative of mettere. An -ere verb takes -a here, which is the ending a friend gets on -are verbs; beside it stands S02's metti.
The polite imperative of dire, and irregular: not dice. It is one of the four polite shapes this module asks you to take whole.

sentences.trap: metta and dica look like nothing else you have met, because they are borrowed from the congiuntivo — the mood L4-M5 opens. Take them as fixed shapes for now.
sentences.sound: SKOO-zee, MET-ta il do-koo-MEN-to sul TA-vo-lo e DEE-ka il NOO-me-ro. dica is DEE-ka: ca is hard.

variations.cue: Put the document on the table
variations.changed: the first order on its own

variations.cue: Put the document on the table — to a friend
variations.changed: familiar, so mettere's -ere swings back to -i

variations.cue: Say the number, please
variations.changed: the second order alone, softened

mistake.display: Scusi, metti il documento sul tavolo
mistake.why: scusi is polite and metti is familiar, so the sentence changes register halfway. Politely it is metta.

sentences.usage: At a counter, a bank window or a doctor's desk.

sentences.display: Senta, apra la porta e aspetti qui
sentences.cue: Excuse me, open the door and wait here
sentences.literal: Listen, open the door and wait here

words.note: The polite imperative of aprire. -ire takes -a here, the exact mirror of S01's apri, which is the same verb spoken to a friend.
The polite imperative of aspettare. -are takes -i here, which is the ending a friend gets on aprire and chiudere: the crossing in one word.

sentences.trap: Both endings are the wrong way round for an English ear: aspetti carries the -i that felt familiar and apra the -a that felt polite. One sentence holds the whole crossing.
sentences.sound: SEN-ta, A-pra la POR-ta e as-PET-tee kwee. apra is stressed on the first syllable, A-pra.

variations.cue: Open the door, please
variations.changed: one order, softened

variations.display: Apri la porta e aspetta qui
variations.cue: Open the door and wait here — to a friend
variations.changed: familiar, and both endings flip over

variations.cue: Excuse me, wait here
variations.changed: just the waiting

mistake.display: Senta, apri la porta e aspetti qui
mistake.why: senta and aspetti are polite; apri is familiar. Politely, aprire takes -a: apra.

sentences.usage: A stranger or an official telling you what to do.
sentences.mnemonic: Polite crosses over: -are takes -i, -ere and -ire take -a.
